{"name": "payments-and-credits", "steps": "Failed card payment
1. lookup_account; ask_developer for invoice_id, error_code, time_of_issue and timezone if not given. Convert the failure time to UTC.
2. search_knowledge for the current payment-failure procedure and for payment-processor incident notices (status cards: "INC card payments failing"). Compare the failure time (UTC) with each published window; the start and end instants count as inside. The time decides, not the decline code.
3. Inside a window: no case. Name the incident, say the payment failed because of it, that it will be retried automatically, when the retries complete, that they need do nothing and no late fees apply. If this notice gives no completion date, derive the processor's usual schedule from ALL past payment-processor notices (search "INC card payments failing" and read each one's window end and "last retries completed" date). For each, call date_calculator(window_end_date, completion_date) and compare calendar_days and business_days; the measure that is the same across every notice is the schedule (a notice ending on a Friday shows whether weekends count). Apply it with date_calculator to this window's end date and state the date. Work this out once, carefully, and keep the same answer on follow-up questions unless you find a notice you had not read.
4. Outside every window, failed again after retries completed, or charged twice after retries: Billing Ops case with invoice number, decline code and failure time (load team-handoff).
5. Bank-transfer / invoice-pay accounts and overdue invoices: search the collections pages for their schedule.

Card changes and card data
- Never ask for, repeat, or store card digits (full, partial, last four, or spoken). If the developer shared one, tell them not to send card details to Support.
- Search the current card-update procedure; follow it (e.g. the customer changes the autopay card themselves in Console billing settings, no case). A card shared during a payment failure doesn't change how the failure is routed.

Credit balances
1. lookup_account: credits are computed from the credit ledger (sum of each grant's entries; expired grants excluded). Search the current credits policy for which table Support quotes.
2. Quote each grant's remaining balance and its own expiry date, plus the total. Mention that credits apply automatically to the next invoice if the policy says so.
3. Cash-out, refund, restoring expired credit or any exception: explain the policy, promise nothing, and open a Finance case only if the developer asks for it (load team-handoff)."}

body: ## Purpose
How Support handles a card payment that failed and a request to change the card used for autopay. Invoice disputes and usage questions are covered on the billing case routing page.
## Failed card payments
If the payment failed inside a published payment-processor incident window, follow Payment Failures During Payment-Processor Incidents instead: no case. Otherwise, open a Billing Ops case with the invoice number, the decline code and the time the payment failed. Billing Ops retries the payment or contacts the customer. Tell the customer Billing Ops has it; don't promise a date."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/payment-failures-during-processor-incidents.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Payment Failures During Payment-Processor Incidents", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-15", "text": "## What to tell the customer

- Say the payment will be retried automatically and when the retries complete, as the processor's usual schedule gives it.
- Say they don't need to do anything, and that no late fees apply to a failure caused by the incident.
- Don't ask for card details. If they want to change the card anyway, they do it in Console billing settings.
## When it still needs a case
- The failure is outside every published incident window.
- The customer tells you the payment failed again after the date the retries complete.
- The customer was charged twice for the same invoice after the retries.
In each of these, open a Billing Ops case as the routing page describes, with the invoice number, the decline code and the time of the failure."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "17/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Exception process

body: ## Inside a published incident window
From 15 March 2027, when there is a published payment-processor incident, a card payment that failed inside the incident window is caused by the incident. Explain the incident to the customer and tell them the payment will be retried automatically, and when the retries complete. Retries follow the processor's usual schedule, which past payment-processor incident notices show. body: ## Scope
Enterprise accounts that pay by bank transfer against net-30 invoices. They have no card on file, so card autopay and processor retries do not apply to them. This page is not about card payments that fail during a payment-processor incident; see the processor incidents page for those.
## Collections
- Billing Ops sends a reminder 5 days after the due date and retries an ACH pull on day 7.
- Questions go to the account team.

- Marketplace charges are issued by Google under the customer’s GCP billing account.
- Redwood usage in the console is near-real-time; Marketplace invoicing may lag due to reporting and billing cycles.
